near_duplicate_a.title: Love Takes Center Stage at the 8th Annual Valentine’s Day Bash at the Manassas Museum
near_duplicate_a.normalized_content: Provided by PWC Circuit Court Clerk’s Office | Photo Credit: Mark Summerson // Mark Summerson Photography – @marksummersonphoto IG On Feb. 14, 2026, hearts will be joined in love as Prince William County Circuit Court Clerk Jacqueline Smith hosts the 8th annual Valentine’s Day Bash at the Manassas Museum. This year’s celebration is anticipated to be the region’s most romantic and captivating Valentine’s Day event of the year, offering couples an elegant and affordable alternative to a traditional wedding. The Valentine’s Day Bash reimagines courtroom-style civil ceremonies with a touch of sophistication, transforming them into unforgettable experiences. More than a nod to Cupid’s arrow, the event celebrates lasting commitments and cherished memories, bringing the community together in a shared moment of happiness. The Manassas Museum’s Mae Merchant Hall will be transformed into a romantic haven, complete with whimsical décor and heart-shaped details. Couples will exchange vows throughout the day in intimate civil ceremonies designed to feel timeless and personal. Every couple’s story adds to the romance of the day. Some pen their own vows, others renew their love after decades of marriage, and others, like former school sweethearts, begin new chapters together. Each ceremony unfolds as a treasured moment, woven into the rich tapestry of love celebrated. “Our Annual Valentine’s Day Bash offers couples a special, elegant, and affordable way to celebrate their union together with family and friends in a welcoming and supportive environment” Jacqueline Smith said. “Our community partners and small businesses come together year after year for this event to make sure all of our couples enjoy every aspect of their very special day.” To schedule your marriage license application and ceremony at the 8th Annual Valentine’s Day Bash, please contact the Circuit Court Clerk’s Office at 703-792-6036 or email CircuitCourt@pwcgov.org. Businesses interested in participating in the event, please reach out to Candi Choi at cchoi@pwcgov.org. The post Love Takes Center Stage at the 8th Annual Valentine’s Day Bash at the Manassas Museum appeared first on Prince William Living.

distinct_a.title: Sealed with Love: Couples Celebrate their Vows at the Circuit Court Clerk’s Winter Wedding Celebration
distinct_a.normalized_content: Provided by Prince William County Circuit Court Clerk’s Office Couples let their love shine this winter amid the charm and warmth of the Town of Occoquan. On Friday, Dec. 12, 2025, Prince William County Circuit Court Clerk Jacqueline C. Smith, in collaboration with the Town of Occoquan, hosted the second annual Seal the Deal, a signature civil wedding experience. Set against Occoquan’s historic streets and waterfront views, the event took place at Madigan’s Waterfront, a fine dining restaurant along the Occoquan River. Nineteen couples exchanged vows in courthouse-style ceremonies beneath a handcrafted arch, surrounded by family and friends. The elegant simplicity of the ceremonies kept the focus on each couple, offering a romantic alternative to traditional wedding planning. Following the ceremonies, couples enjoyed celebratory refreshments and “wedding cupcakes” at Madigan’s. Local businesses contributed to the festivities, transforming Seal the Deal into a full community celebration. The Circuit Court Clerk’s Office extends gratitude to the Town of Occoquan and the local business community for their generosity in providing wedding gifts to the couples. Contributions came from Madigan’s Waterfront, Ballywhack Shack, Brandon’s Flowers, Curate, Evidi Massage, Forever Young, Glory Be, Hello Jackson, Hitchcock Paper, Jerry’s Occoquan Jewelers, Leaf & Petal, Mark Summerson Photography, and Occoquan Outfitter. Together, these partners helped create a day where love stories unfolded in a town sparkling with romance, community, and holiday magic. In February 2026, the Clerk will host her annual Valentine’s Day Bash, inviting couples to come together once again for romantic civil unions. For updates and information about civil ceremony events, follow @PWCCircuitCourt on social media or visit pwcva.gov/department/circuit-court. distinct_b.title: Fall Focus on Fruit: Persimmons
distinct_b.normalized_content: Provided by Cakes by Happy Eatery Persimmons are orange fruits that are in season in the fall and winter featuring multiple varieties that originated in China centuries ago.  There are two main varieties: the fuyu persimmon looks like an orange squat tomato or a miniature pumpkin, and the hachiya persimmon is larger and elongated (kind of like a big, orange acorn) or heart shaped. Both varieties are sweet when ripe and taste like a cross between a papaya and a peach.  Emily Wu-Rorrer of Cakes By Happy Eatery went on Fox 5’s Good Day DC earlier today to demonstrate some of the best ways to take advantage of this cool weather treat. One important difference between the two varieties: fresh fuyu is non-astringent and can be eaten firm or ripe, almost like an apple with a peach/mango flavor.  Hachiya is very astringent and must be eaten ripe, otherwise Wu-Rorrer says “your mouth will experience a dry, puckering sensation and even feel a little numb!”.  Once ripe, persimmons to not keep well, so enjoy quickly! “We love baking with them,” says Wu-Rorrer.  “You want to puree the ripe fruit with the skin on, and blend into a pulp.  I like to do bread or muffins with them.”  The bakery also likes to do an upside-down cake with them similar to the pineapple version or broil them halved and drizzled with honey.  Persimmon pie is also an option and presents similar to pumpkin. Once you’ve exhausted your baking options and still have some left, why not do a smoothie?  Wu-Rorrer says slice of the stem, cut into wedges (keep the skin if ripe), and then she likes to go with a milk alternative like almond, oat or soy milk with some cinnamon or nutmeg. For more information about persimmons and other seasonal options, click here.  You can also follow the bakery on Instagram or Facebook.
